title: Regulating Greenwashing: Where Market Rules Meet Climate Action
content: Tinned tomatoes that have ‘zero climate change impact’.11 Gardening compost that is ‘climate neutral’.22 Drinks that are ‘carbon-negative’.33 These are but a few examples of products currently available on the market making environmental claims. The fact that the list of such goods is rapidly increasing shouldn’t come as a surprise. Consumers’ sustainability demands are similarly rising44 with the effect that ‘green’ products are seeing ‘greater growth than standard products’.55 In other words, companies are incentivised to commit to ‘green’ production and products, and to market their business as such.
